name: MsFLASH Vaginal Health Trial
aliases: Menopause Strategies: Finding Lasting Answers for Symptoms and Health Vaginal Health Trial
question: Do vaginal estradiol tablets or a vaginal moisturizer reduce bothersome postmenopausal vulvovaginal symptoms more than dual placebo?

design.blinding: Double-blind; participants, study personnel, and clinicians masked

arms.label: Vaginal 10-μg estradiol tablet plus placebo gel
placebo tablet plus Replens vaginal moisturizer

design.population: Women aged 45–70 years at least two years after their last menses, with at least one moderate or severe weekly vulvovaginal symptom or monthly pain with vaginal penetration.
design.locator: Mitchell 2018 full text, Methods: Study Design, Patient Selection, Interventions; Results: Figure 1

verdictNote: Neither active arm met the prespecified MBS superiority threshold; estradiol improved secondary menopause-related quality of life.
takeaway: In the MsFLASH Vaginal Health Trial, vaginal 10-μg estradiol tablets plus placebo gel and Replens moisturizer plus placebo tablets did not reduce 12-week most-bothersome-symptom severity more than dual placebo tablets and gel.

reports.label: Primary symptom report
reports.citation: Mitchell CM, Reed SD, Diem S, et al. "Efficacy of Vaginal Estradiol or Vaginal Moisturizer vs Placebo for Treating Postmenopausal Vulvovaginal Symptoms: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA Intern Med.* 2018;178(5):681-690. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2018.0116
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods: Study Design and Data Collection

results.note: Prespecified two-sided alpha 0.025 for each active-versus-placebo comparison; P value from repeated-measures model across weeks 4 and 12.

delivery.value: Vagifem or matching tablet daily for 2 weeks, then twice weekly for 10 weeks; Replens or hydroxyethylcellulose placebo gel every 3 days.
